claims.explanation: Gabazine is a competitive GABA-A receptor antagonist, and its selective toxicity across cancer lines most plausibly reflects dependence on GABA-A receptor subunit expression (especially GABRA3/GABRA5 and GABRG2) for autocrine/paracrine proliferative or survival signaling, so lines with high receptor expression are sensitized while low-expressors are protected. The enrichment of TP53 and RAS/PI3K pathway mutations among sensitive lines suggests that loss of p53 and activated MAPK/PI3K signaling cooperate with GABA-A blockade to trigger apoptosis, whereas intact survival signaling (e.g., EGFR-mutant or PTEN-mutant lines) buffers against it.

features.basis: GABRA3 is a core gabazine target and is overexpressed in many carcinomas where GABA-A signaling promotes proliferation/migration
GABRA5-containing receptors are gabazine-sensitive and drive GABAergic trophic signaling in tumors
GABRG2 is required for functional gabazine-sensitive GABA-A receptor complexes
TP53 mutation is nearly universal in the most-killed lines, consistent with loss of apoptosis checkpoint allowing GABA-A blockade to kill
KRAS-mutant lines (OV7, T3M4, SNUC5, KYSE510) are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven dependence on GABA-A survival signals
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines (LOXIMVI, IGR37, SNUC5) appear among sensitive lines
PTEN loss (ZR751, FTC133, KALS1) is enriched in sensitive lines, implicating PI3K-AKT dependence
SMARCA4 mutations appear in several sensitive lines (OV7, KYSE270), suggesting chromatin-remodeling vulnerability
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) are among the least affected, indicating EGFR survival signaling buffers GABA-A blockade
High GABRA1-containing synaptic-type receptors may be less coupled to proliferative signaling, reducing gabazine toxicity
Beta subunits are obligate for GABA-A channel function and gabazine binding; expression marks responsive tumors
GABRA2 is a gabazine target whose expression may mark receptor-addicted lines
